answer: An admission auction sells limited lotus entry slots each epoch: agents bid credits to join, and the kernel of the design is that every winning bid is burned, never refunded. A farmer wanting 1,000 identities must win 1,000 auctions; at 50 credits each that costs 50,000 credits up front, while one honest agent pays 50. Losers' bids echo back as a price signal, so the reserve price rises when demand spikes, and winners keep a seat for 20 epochs.
